title: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet I (Gilgamesh and the creation of Enkidu): tablet K.2756.C
source: British Museum K.2756.C photograph via eBL + eBL manuscript ATF (L.1.4 SB I) + R. Campbell Thompson 1928
description: Standard Babylonian Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet I, as written on British Museum tablet K.2756.C (Nineveh, Library of Ashurbanipal, 7th c. BCE; George 2003 manuscript B₃; K.2756C, column i). 16 lines preserved in column(s) i. Akkadian is the eBL transliteration of this tablet; English is R. Campbell Thompson (1928).
introduction:
Tablet I of the Epic of Gilgamesh (Standard Babylonian version, attributed to Sin-leqi-unninni) as it survives on one physical object: British Museum tablet K.2756.C (K.2756C, column i), excavated at Nineveh from the library of Ashurbanipal (7th c. BCE). It is manuscript B₃ in A. R. George's 2003 edition. The photograph is the British Museum's, showing the inscribed face(s) and edges; column(s) i are preserved (16 lines).

Three criteria are met for every section:

  1. Manuscript scan: the British Museum photograph of K.2756.C itself (served by the Electronic Babylonian Library, LMU Munich). Each section names the column and face (obverse = columns i-iii, reverse = columns iv-vi) and the tablet's own line numbers, so the reader can find the lines on the photograph.
  2. Original text: the eBL manuscript-level ATF transliteration of the signs on this tablet (not the composite text). Brackets [ ] mark broken signs, x an illegible sign, # a damaged sign. Superscript numbers are the modern line numbers of George 2003 / eBL.
  3. Public-domain English: R. Campbell Thompson, The Epic of Gilgamish (London, 1928), verbatim, with his marginal line numbers as T n.

On line numbers. Thompson's 1928 numbering is not George's. For Tablet I the eBL edition records Thompson's 1930 column/line number for each modern line, and that concordance is used here. Where the tablet's text begins or ends inside a Thompson block, the whole block is given and the section says so. Thompson's readings reflect the state of knowledge in 1928: modern editions (George 2003; the eBL edition, updated continuously) supersede him and are not public domain, so they are not reproduced here beyond the transliteration of this tablet's signs.

translation.text:
(The Argument).

T i 1He who (the heart of) all matters hath proven let him [teach] the nation,
[He who all] knowledge possesseth, therein shall he [school] all the people,
[He shall his wisdom impart (?)] and (so) shall they ]share it] together.
[Gilgamish(?)] —he was the [Master] of wisdom, with [knowledge of all things,

T i 5He ’twas discovered the secret concealed . . . . . . . . .
(Aye), handed down the tradition relating to (things) prediluvian,
Went on a journey afar, (all) aweary and [worn with his toiling(?)],

translation.text:
T i 10[Graved] on a table of stone all the travail.
Of Erech, the high-wall’d,
He (it was) built up the ramparts; (and) he (it was) clamp’d the foundation,
Like unto brass, of [E]-Anna , the sacred, the treasury hallow’d,
[Strengthen’d] its base to grant wayleave to no [one] . . . . . .
. . . . . the threshold which from [of old (?)] . . . . . .
. . . . . [E]-Anna . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

T i 15. . . . . to grant wayleave [to no one (?)] . . . . . . .

(About thirty lines wanting. The description of Gilgamish runs on to the beginning of the next Column).

Thompson's numbered block(s) extend after the lines preserved on this tablet; the whole block is given so that no English line is cut mid-block.
